{"id": "24772869-56c7-4159-a978-dd8214a6d535", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_HLIWTXJfNwfXFqMd4lF3SO", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Agent Replay\\\\n\\\\nA replay is a new investigation that re-runs a finished one. It re-sends the original\\'s title and description, and it reasons only about the original\\'s time window. A replay is read-only: it cannot be steered, forked or mitigated, and it changes nothing in the customer\\'s systems. Never say a replay changed, fixed or restarted anything.\\\\n\\\\nThe original and all of its replays are one family. A replay of a replay does not exist: always replay the original.\\\\n\\\\n## Find the runs\\\\n\\\\n- `[Now viewing: investigation/<originalId>/compare/<replayId>]`: the first id is the original, the second is a replay.\\\\n- `[Now viewing: investigation/<id>]`: call `list_replays(id)`. It works from the original or from any replay, and tells you which is the original.\\\\n- Otherwise use the ids from the conversation, or ask the user. Never guess an id.\\\\n\\\\n## Start a replay\\\\n\\\\n1. Read the original with `get_investigation`.\\\\n2. Before `start_replay`, always confirm with the user. Do not ask the user for a lookback first: use 60 minutes unless the user named one. If the user names a lookback `start_replay` does not accept, use the nearest one it accepts and say so in the confirm. Show:\\\\n   - the prompt that will be re-sent: the original\\'s title and description, as they are;\\\\n   - the window: it starts `lookback_minutes` before the original was created and ends when the original\\'s run ended. Say the user can pick another lookback `start_replay` accepts instead;\\\\n   - the note, if any.\\\\n   Ask for a clear yes. Do not call `start_replay` until the user says yes.\\\\n3. Call `start_replay(original_task_id, lookback_minutes, note)`.\\\\n4. On success, say the replay started and give both links from the result: `replay_link` for the replay itself and `compare_link` for the compare page. When `window_past_retention` is true, say the window is older than 14 days, so some logs and metrics may be gone and the replay may see less data. When `reference_dropped` is true, say the original\\'s ticket link was not valid, so the replay has none.\\\\n5. On a refusal, say why in plain words and what the user can do:\\\\n   - the task is a replay: offer to replay its original;\\\\n   - the original is not finished: it can be replayed once it ends;\\\\n   - `active_replay_exists`: one replay of it is still running; wait for it to finish;\\\\n   - `rate_limited`: try again later;\\\\n   - `unavailable`: replays are not available here;\\\\n   - `note_too_long`: offer a shorter note.\\\\n\\\\n## List replays\\\\n\\\\nCall `list_replays(task_id)`. Name each replay \\\\\"Replay N\\\\\" by its `number`, with its note when it has one, and give its status and created time. Say which replays have a review (`graded`); only those can be picked on the compare page.\\\\n\\\\n## Compare two runs\\\\n\\\\nCompare the original with a replay, or two replays of the same original.\\\\n\\\\n1. Both runs must be finished. If one is still running, say so and offer to compare once it ends.\\\\n2. Call `compare_runs(task_a, task_b)`. Pass the original (or the older replay) as `task_a`.\\\\n3. Explain, in this order:\\\\n   - the grade: each run\\'s quality level, and whether it got better, worse or stayed the same (`deltas.grade`);\\\\n   - each dimension that changed (`deltas.dimensions_changed`), with each run\\'s justification for it from `a.grade.justifications` and `b.grade.justifications`;\\\\n   - the root causes: whether both runs found the same root cause, and how they differ;\\\\n   - the duration change (`deltas.duration_minutes`; shorter is better);\\\\n   - tools and skills only one run used, and big changes in tool counts.\\\\n   A run with grade status `reviewing` or `not_reviewed` has no grade yet: say so, and compare the rest.\\\\n4. Add the caveats that apply:\\\\n   - always: the runs used the agent\\'s memory and skills as they were when each ran, and those may have changed since the original;\\\\n   - `caveats.retention`: the replay\\'s window was older than 14 days when it ran, so it may have seen less data;\\\\n   - `caveats.other_source_run`: the replay was made from an earlier run of the original;\\\\n   - `journal_truncated` on a run: its tool and skill counts are partial.\\\\n5. Give the `compare_link` from the result. For two replays it opens the newer replay\\'s compare page; tell the user to pick the other replay in the page\\'s run selector.\\\\n\\\\n## Links\\\\n\\\\n- Compare page: `[[replay_compare:<originalTaskId>:<replayTaskId>:<title>]]`, exactly as the tools return it in `compare_link`.\\\\n- One run: `[[investigation:<task_id>:<title>]]`.\"}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_2ISrGy4QTDnvZ0x956qSI9", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Review Results\\\\n\\\\nEach completed investigation can be assessed by an automated reviewer against a\\\\nquality rubric. A review has an overall quality level (**helpful** or\\\\n**unhelpful**) and a set of per-dimension verdicts, each **pass**, **fail**, or\\\\n**not applicable**, with a one-sentence justification per dimension. A review\\\\nalso includes the stated root cause of the investigation.\\\\n\\\\n**The dimensions are configurable per agent space** \\\\u2014 a customer can edit the\\\\ngrading rubric (add, remove, or rename dimensions) via the grader\\'s `AGENTS.md`.\\\\nSo treat the dimension set as dynamic: report whatever dimensions each review\\\\nactually carries, and never assume a fixed list. The common default dimensions\\\\nare:\\\\n\\\\n- **Scope alignment** \\\\u2014 did the investigation address the actual alarm/problem?\\\\n- **Evidence grounding** \\\\u2014 are the conclusions backed by evidence?\\\\n- **Investigation completeness** \\\\u2014 can oncall act on the result?\\\\n- **Environment impact** \\\\u2014 do the deterministic signals support the verdict?\\\\n\\\\nA given agent space may have fewer, more, or differently named dimensions.\\\\n\\\\n**The rubric is editable.** The grading rubric lives in a **GRADER-scoped AGENTS.md**\\\\n(`agent_type` **GRADER**). To reset to the built-in defaults, delete the GRADER\\\\nAGENTS.md.\\\\n\\\\n## Viewing Results of All Reviews\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-1: Summarize all reviews\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `list_grader_results`. Each entry is one completed review, carrying the\\\\n   reviewed investigation\\'s title (`investigationTitle`) and its `grade`. Use\\\\n   `createdAfter` / `createdBefore` for time-bounded requests (\\\\\"reviews from last\\\\n   week\\\\\"). Only reviewed investigations appear \\\\u2014 an unreviewed one has no entry.\\\\n2. If a `next_token` is returned and the user wants the full picture, page through\\\\n   with it before summarizing counts.\\\\n4. When a dimension failed, lead with the failing dimension and its\\\\n   reasoning.\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer the full list of reviews or to open the investigation itself.\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-4: Previous / earlier reviews of one investigation\\\\n\\\\nAn investigation is usually reviewed once, but a re-review produces additional\\\\nreviews. To retrieve them:\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `get_grader_result` with the investigation\\'s task id and\\\\n   `include_history: true`. See the tool\\'s own description for the exact response\\\\n   fields (current review plus the earlier ones and a total count).\\\\n2. If there are no earlier reviews, tell the user this investigation has only been\\\\n   reviewed once. Do not treat that as an error.\\\\n   **But** if the response also has `scan_window_exhausted: true`, the history may\\\\n   be incomplete (older reviews fell outside the scanned window) \\\\u2014 say the earlier\\\\n   reviews shown may not be the full history rather than asserting there was only\\\\n   one review.\\\\n3. When the user wants a comparison, contrast the current grade against the most\\\\n   recent previous one: call out quality-level changes (e.g. UNHELPFUL \\\\u2192 HELPFUL)\\\\n   and any dimension verdict that flipped, with the reasoning for each.\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer to open the investigation or list all reviews.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Shared Guidance\\\\n\\\\n## Not-Yet-Reviewed Investigations\\\\n\\\\n- When `get_grader_result` reports no review for an investigation, tell the user it\\\\n  hasn\\'t been reviewed yet \\\\u2014 do not treat this as an error, and do not invent a grade.\\\\n- **But** when the tool\\'s response indicates its scan window was exhausted (see the\\\\n  tool description), do NOT say the investigation was never reviewed. Relay the tool\\'s\\\\n  own message \\\\u2014 a review may exist but is older \\\\u2014 and offer to narrow by time or open\\\\n  the investigation directly.\\\\n- When a listed review reports it couldn\\'t be loaded, skip it in your counts and, if\\\\n  relevant, note that one review couldn\\'t be loaded rather than failing the whole\\\\n  summary.\\\\n\\\\n## Tool Errors\\\\n\\\\nIf `list_grader_results` or `get_grader_result` returns an \\\\\"Unknown tool\\\\\" result:\\\\n\\\\n- The skill\\'s tools were dropped from this session. Call\\\\n  `skill_read(\\\\\"review-results\\\\\")` ONCE to reload them, then retry the original tool\\\\n  call ONCE.\\\\n- This is NOT an access/permission problem \\\\u2014 do not tell the user the feature is\\\\n  unavailable.\\\\n\\\\nOnly if a tool returns an explicit access-denied / authorization error (a\\\\npermissions message, not \\\\\"Unknown tool\\\\\"):\\\\n\\\\n- Do NOT retry the call.\\\\n- Explain the feature may not be enabled for their account.\\\\n\\\\n## Capability Boundaries\\\\n\\\\n- You CAN list reviews across investigations and open a single investigation\\'s\\\\n  review.\\\\n- You CAN summarize review results and compose an artifact from them.\\\\n- You CANNOT create, edit, re-run, or delete a review \\\\u2014 reviews are produced by a\\\\n  separate reviewer process, not on demand. {"id": "eff808b0-c933-4a02-86b1-f7ff504cb361", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You can use replay. It re-runs a finished investigation under your current configuration, so the old investigation becomes your "before" and the replay becomes your "after".

**How it works**
1. Pick completed investigations that ran under the old prompt. A replay re-sends the original's title and description and reasons only about the original's time window.
2. Replay each one after the new prompt is live. Replays are read-only and don't change the originals or your systems.
3. Compare each original with its replay on:
   - review grade (helpful or unhelpful, plus pass or fail per dimension)
   - root cause found
   - time to root cause
   - tools and skills used

**The old investigations need reviews.** A comparison is only as useful as the grades on both sides. Reviews can't be run on demand. They run automatically on a sample of completed investigations (10% by default), when a linked ServiceNow or PagerDuty ticket is resolved, or 7 days after completion. Some of your old investigations may already have one. If a replay has a grade and its original doesn't, you still get the root cause, time and tool comparison, but no grade comparison.

**Limits to keep in mind**
- **Data retention:** replays query your live environment. Logs and metrics older than about 14 days may be gone, so the replay may see less data than the original did. Prefer recent investigations.
- **Other changes:** the replay uses your current skills and memories. If anything besides the prompt changed since the original, the comparison reflects that too.
- **Sample size:** one pair is an anecdote. Use 10 or more varied investigations, including ones the old prompt handled well, and look at the pattern across all of them.
- **Grading rubric:** keep it the same for both runs. If you change it between runs, the grades aren't comparable.

I can list your recent completed investigations and check which ones already have reviews. That would give us a shortlist of good candidates to replay. I'd confirm the prompt and window with you before starting any replay.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
